mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS rise, or credit spreads widen but SPX does not decline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 50,000 jobs predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative despite the PAYEMS increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1.2% growth over the prior two months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be positive, reflecting stronger consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth > 1.2% over the previous two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the HOUST acceleration, or the effect is not robust across multiple backtests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to weak manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (current value - 2%) for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the INDPRO contraction, or the effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting reduced labor market friction and improved growth prospects.
failure_condition: Forward returns remain flat or negative despite the unemployment decline, or the effect is not robust in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 3% and 4% respectively over the next quarter are expected to drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return through stronger aggregate demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (current value * 1.03) AND RSAFS > (current value * 1.04) over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not positive, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% for the next month predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes and equity discount rates widen.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive despite the inflation spike, or the effect is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of FEDFUNDS > 4% and INDPRO < (current value - 1%) for two months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative, reflecting persistent monetary tightening and weak supply growth.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4 AND INDPRO < (current value - 1) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is positive despite the combined trigger, or the interaction is not statistically significant.
